title: Nephrologist visit
what: A doctor who treats kidney conditions and helps keep your kidneys working.
why: For abnormal urine or blood tests, swelling, high blood pressure, kidney disease, or diabetes affecting the kidneys.
tell_doctor: All your medicines, including painkillers and supplements
Any swelling or changes in your urine

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Bring all your urine and blood tests, especially creatinine, and your kidney ultrasound.

prepare.title: Blood pressure
prepare.text: If you check it at home, bring your blood pressure diary.

bring: Past test results, discharge papers, and reports
A list of your medicines, or the packs themselves
steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms and medicines
Your blood pressure and weight are checked
Your tests and ultrasound are reviewed
feel: Nothing unpleasant. It is a regular checkup
You may be asked to give a urine sample the same day
after: Best not to take painkillers or supplements without your doctor. Ask first
red_flags: You have almost stopped passing urine, or have severe swelling or shortness of breath: call emergency services

faq.q: What tests does a nephrologist need?
faq.a: Usually a urine test, blood creatinine, and a kidney ultrasound. Your doctor will give the exact list.

faq.q: Can I take painkillers with kidney disease?
faq.a: Not all of them. Ask your doctor which ones suit you.

reminders.text: Nephrologist visit tomorrow. Bring your blood and urine tests, ultrasound, and blood pressure diary.
